questions.q: How did the Badger's voice change when he learned who was at the door?
choices: It went from gruff and suspicious to warm and welcoming
It went from friendly to angry
It stayed cold and unfriendly
It became frightened and quiet
questions.evidence: exclaimed the Badger, in quite a different voice

questions.q: What was the Badger wearing when he opened the door?
choices: A long dressing-gown and down-at-heel slippers
A heavy winter coat and boots
A smoking-suit of black velvet
Nothing but his fur
questions.evidence: The Badger, who wore a long dressing-gown

questions.q: Which room did the Badger lead his cold visitors into first?
choices: A large fire-lit kitchen
His study
A cold stone cellar
The bedroom loft
questions.evidence: the glow and warmth of a large fire-lit kitchen

questions.q: Why did the Mole begin to feel very friendly toward the Badger during supper?
choices: The Badger listened without scolding or saying 'I told you so'
The Badger gave him a present
The Badger praised his bravery
The Badger promised to visit him on the river
questions.evidence: he never said, 'I told you so,'

questions.q: According to the Rat, how was Toad getting on with his motor-cars?
choices: From bad to worse, with his seventh smash-up
Very well, he had become a careful driver
He had given up motor-cars for good
He had won a motor-car race

questions.q: What did the Rat fear would happen to Toad if he kept driving?
choices: He would end up killed or ruined
He would become too famous
He would move away from the river
He would forget his old friends
questions.evidence: Killed or ruined--it's got to be one of the two things

questions.q: Why did the Badger say he could not do anything about Toad right now?
choices: It was winter, when animals rest and are not expected to do anything active
He was too old to help
He did not care about Toad
Toad had moved away

questions.q: Why did the Mole feel lively in Badger's house while the Rat kept falling asleep?
choices: The Mole was an underground animal, so the house suited him
The Mole had drunk a lot of coffee
The Rat had walked much further that day
The Mole was afraid to fall asleep
questions.evidence: he being naturally an underground animal by birth and breeding

questions.q: Who were eating porridge at the Badger's table the next morning?
choices: Two young hedgehogs who had lost their way to school
Two rabbits from the Wild Wood
The Otter and his son
Two weasels
questions.evidence: we was trying to find our way to school

questions.q: When the hedgehog said Mr. Badger was "busy" in his study, what was the Badger really doing?
choices: Napping in an arm-chair with a handkerchief over his face
Writing a letter to Toad
Counting his winter stores
Planning an attack on the weasels
questions.evidence: a red cotton handkerchief over his face

questions.q: Who arrived at Badger's front door while the friends were at breakfast?
choices: The Otter
Toad
The hedgehogs' mother
A policeman
questions.evidence: Billy returned in front of the Otter

questions.q: What did the Otter think of the rabbits for not helping the Mole?
choices: He was disgusted that so many of them did nothing
He said they were wise to stay hidden
He praised them for trying hard
He did not care at all
questions.evidence: "What, US?" he merely said: "DO something? us rabbits?"

questions.q: What did the Mole and the Badger agree about at lunch?
choices: Living underground gives the most peace and security
The river is the best place to live
Toad Hall is the finest home of all
Winter is the best season
questions.evidence: There's no security, or peace and tranquillity, except underground.

questions.q: Who had built the great passages, halls and arches of Badger's home?
choices: People of an ancient city that once stood there
The Badger himself, over many years
The Badger's grandfather
The weasels and stoats
questions.evidence: there was a city--a city of people, you know

questions.q: The Badger says badgers "are an enduring lot." What does "enduring" mean here?
choices: Lasting a long time and always coming back
Easily tired
Very wealthy
Fond of travel

questions.q: What did the Badger promise the Mole about the Wild Wood?
choices: He would pass the word around so the Mole would have no more trouble
He would chase all the weasels away forever
He would never let the Mole visit again
He would build the Mole a house there
questions.evidence: Any friend of MINE walks where he likes in this country

questions.q: How did the friends get out of the Wild Wood at the end of the visit?
choices: Through one of Badger's long tunnels to the edge of the wood
Riding in Toad's motor-car
By following the river in the Otter's boat
Across the snow on a door-mat sled
questions.evidence: you shall leave by one of my short cuts

questions.q: What does the Mole realize about himself at the end of the chapter?
choices: He belongs to the pleasant fields and hedgerows, not the wild rough places
He wants to live in the Wild Wood with Badger
He wants to travel the Wide World
He should learn to drive a motor-car
questions.evidence: the Mole saw clearly that he was an animal of tilled field and hedge-row
